question.prompt:
In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(D\) is a point on side \(\overline{AC}\) such that \(BD=DC\) and \(\angle BCD\) measures \(70^\circ.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle ADB?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_8_Q09_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The useful triangle is \(BDC\): since \(BD=DC\), it is isosceles with base \(BC\). The angles opposite those equal sides are equal, so
\[
\angle DBC=\angle BCD=70^\circ.
\]
Because \(A,D,C\) are collinear with \(D\) between \(A\) and \(C\), \(DA\) extends \(DC\). Thus \(\angle ADB\) is an exterior angle of \(\triangle BDC\). An exterior angle equals the sum of the two nonadjacent interior angles, giving
\[
\angle ADB=70^\circ+70^\circ
=\boxed{140^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Equal base angles and an exterior angle
